evidence.note: HEAD-header test failure led to inspecting s3_objects.py, a targeted edit, and a clean-state re-run — cause diagnosed and fixed, not symptom-patched.

Edge-test URL-encoding failure: investigated boto3 space-key encoding, did a roundtrip check, fixed the core sigv4 module, then ran the full regression suite to confirm dependents — a foundational signing correction with re-verification (anchor-8 pattern).
Clock-skew auth failure: manually crafted a skewed valid signature to isolate whether the test or app was wrong, correctly attributing it to the test — disciplined diagnosis before changing anything.

Audit double-logging: verified one-line-per-request, refactored logging across app.py and s3_api.py, then re-verified no double-logging on success and missing-bucket — design-level correction with dependent re-verification.
Notification signing failures diagnosed to the test harness's signing rather than blindly patching the app.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly treats verification failures as signal, diagnosing the actual cause (frequently distinguishing its own test bugs from app bugs), and in at least two cases makes module/design-level corrections (the sigv4 URL-encoding fix and the audit-logging refactor) followed by regression re-verification of dependents — squarely between anchors 5 and 8. It falls short of a full 8-10 because no foundational storage/concurrency assumption was ever falsified requiring a decisive structural pivot, so the highest-altitude corrective behavior is not demonstrated.
